item.description:
What's new in 1.0.0

  • Free during early access: no weekly limit, no subscription section, no account. A paid plan comes later.
  • One speech model: NVIDIA Parakeet v3, 461 MB, 25 European languages. It listens while you speak, and the last piece is on screen well under a second after you let go.
  • Text is tidied by rules — filler words out, punctuation in, your word list applied — instantly, and no word can be lost. The language-model cleanup and its 2.4 GB download are gone.
  • Settings reduced to what matters: language, speech model, clean up, word list, keys, agent, updates, diagnostics.
  • Recordings send more frames: up to 40 for long videos, sampled every half second, so what you show quickly is in the picture. Frames that don't fit the agent's context are listed with time and reason, ready to fetch one by one.
  • New icon: the four corners of a viewfinder and a wave for the voice.
  • Every dictation keeps its audio. Listen to it or transcribe it again from the History.
  • Double-tap ⌘ takes a screenshot, double-tap ⌥ starts and stops a recording, one tap on ⌥ (right) marks a spot while recording, fn dictates.
  • Diagnostics: copy the log of one dictation, or a timing report with the median per step.
  • Cueshot updates itself: it checks once a day, shows you what's new, and installs on your say-so — or on its own, if you turn that on under Updates. Your agent keeps working, because the MCP server travels inside the app.
